title_en: UGO13: How Much Longer Can AI Carry the Market ft. Christian Mueller-Glissmann
title_zh: UGO13：AI还能撑住市场多久？——对话高盛 Christian Mueller-Glissmann
subtitle_zh: 高盛资产配置研究主管 Christian Mueller-Glissmann 与主持人 Cem Karsan 深入探讨 AI 资本开支繁荣下的盈利泡沫与估值泡沫之争、债市的‘限速’、波动率与市场分化，以及货币贬值时代的资产配置之道。
description: UGO13: How Much Longer Can AI Carry the Market ft. Christian Mueller-Glissmann

turns.en: Welcome back to U Got Options from the Cboe floor brought to you by Top Traders Unplugged and Kai Media. today we get to talk to Christian Mueller-Glissmann, from Goldman Sachs. An incredibly wide-ranging conversation dealing with everything from are we in a bubble? Are the earnings real and sustainable in

What's the role of volatility in a portfolio and are we likely, at this point, to need to look at vol a little bit more than we had been in previous periods? Lastly, where are we going with the bond market and the speed limit of 60/40? Is this a time to

Today I get Christian Mueller-Glissmann, from Goldman Sachs. He's the head of asset allocation research there. We have talked once before quite a while
turns.zh: 保持警惕、并为货币贬值（debasement）做好准备了呢？我想你一定会非常喜欢这一期。（音乐）欢迎收看《U Got Options》在Cboe交易现场为您带来的又一期节目。今天我请到了来自高盛（Goldman Sachs）的Christian Mueller-Glissmann，他是那里的资产配置研究主管。我们此前对谈过一次，那是很久

turns.zh: 以前了，上次那场对话非常精彩。迫不及待想今天再聊一次，欢迎你，Christian。感谢邀请，Cem，我也很期待。

turns.en: So, I want to start out today with a couple concepts you have very recently kind of been talking about which is how the bond market has really been kind of… is becoming the speed limit of the equity market and this concept of broadly kind of innovation versus inflation. There's really this tension between these, the bond market
turns.zh: 那么，今天我想先从你近期一直在谈的几个概念说起，也就是债市实际上如何正在……成为股票市场的‘限速’（speed limit），以及那个更宏观的‘创新对抗通胀’（innovation versus inflation）的理念。在这两者之间——债市与

turns.en: and the stock market, and what's happening. If you wouldn't mind maybe take us through a little bit of kind of how you're thinking about this moment we're in in terms of growth versus inflation, etc. And I'd love to hear a little bit kind of about how you see asset allocation at this time in history.
turns.zh: 股市之间，以及正在发生的情况——确实存在这种张力。如果你不介意，或许可以带我们梳理一下，在增长与通胀等方面，你如何看待我们当下所处的这个时刻。我也很想听听在这个历史节点上你如何看待资产配置。

turns.en: Yeah, sure. I mean listen, I think this macro regime that we have since the beginning of the year is very different to what most people expected coming into the year. Like at the beginning of the year like you had unemployment rates that were low, profit margins were high, equity valuations were elevated,
turns.zh: 好的，当然。我是说，听着，我认为今年以来我们所处的这个宏观格局（macro regime），与大多数人年初时的预期非常不同。因为在年初，你有低失业率、高利润率、股票估值高企，

turns.en: policy rates were somewhat high and the best people were hoping for was some type of Goldilocks market where you get a bit of inflation relief coupled with maybe some regulatory and fiscal kind of help from policymakers. But instead, you got this enormous AI CapEx boom that really pushed the business cycle
turns.zh: 政策利率也处于相对高位，人们所能期盼的最好情形，不过是某种‘金发姑娘’（Goldilocks）式市场——即通胀有所缓解，再加上政策制定者在监管和财政方面给予一些帮助。但结果，你却迎来了这场规模巨大的AI资本开支（AI CapEx）繁荣，它在一定程度上把商业周期

turns.en: to some extent back into a mid-cycle acceleration. Like, you create this enormous releveraging and you have to consider that the only thing that didn't look very late-cycle at the end of last year was private sector leverage. Like the private sector didn't look particularly leveraged. And now you
turns.zh: 重新推回了周期中段（mid-cycle）的加速阶段。也就是说，你创造了这种规模巨大的再杠杆化（releveraging），而且你必须考虑到，去年年底唯一看起来不那么‘周期末段’的东西，就是私营部门的杠杆。也就是说，私营部门当时看起来并没有特别高的杠杆。而现在你

turns.en: get a major re-leveraging here with the AI CapEx boom. And this AI CapEx boom has created this nominal growth acceleration. And that already feeds into the bond market. Because if you get like nominal growth accelerated, that usually is good for equities, it's bad for bonds. And equities are usually supported by
turns.zh: 在AI资本开支繁荣中迎来了一轮重大的再杠杆化。而这场AI资本开支繁荣创造了这种名义增长（nominal growth）的加速。这已经传导到了债市。因为如果名义增长加速，那通常利好股票、利空债券。而股票通常又受到

turns.en: better earnings growth. And we've seen some of that for sure, even though it's been very narrowly driven. But we've had significant upward revisions to earnings growth. And then obviously, on the bond side, you have the issue that often such an acceleration can drive inflation. And I think this time around, a lot of the inflation
turns.zh: 更好的盈利增长的支撑。这一点我们确实看到了一些，尽管它的驱动面非常狭窄。但我们确实看到了对盈利增长的大幅上修。然后显然，在债券这一侧，你面临的问题是，这种加速往往会推高通胀。而我认为这一次，很多通胀

turns.en: has actually maybe not even been driven by the AI CapEx boom, some of it. But I think the bigger driver of inflation has been the Middle East war. So, the Middle East war pushing up energy prices has then boosted inflation. And now the bond market essentially has to adjust to this new macro regime. Equities have
turns.zh: 实际上也许并不完全是由AI资本开支繁荣驱动的，只有一部分是。但我认为通胀更大的推手是中东战争。所以，中东战争推高能源价格，进而抬升了通胀。而现在债市本质上必须去适应这个新的宏观格局。股票则已经

turns.en: already kind of, to some extent, reaped some of the benefits because you had the earnings growth really boosting equities. But I think the bond market is still trying to find its new equilibrium. And as you were saying, the risk you're facing is a bit as the earnings tailwinds for equities are kind of moderating a
turns.zh: 在一定程度上、某种层面上收获了一些好处，因为盈利增长确实在提振股市。但我认为债市仍在试图寻找它新的均衡点。正如你所说，你面临的风险有点像是——随着股票的盈利顺风在一定程度上开始减弱，

turns.en: bit because they've been really enormous for the first half of the year. The rates headwinds are starting to bite a bit, and they're starting to weigh on equities a bit, especially certain parts of equities. And I guess that's the speed limit that you're talking about. The speed of the bond selloff, coupled
turns.zh: 因为它们在上半年的确非常强劲。利率的逆风开始产生影响了，开始对股票构成一定的压制，尤其是股市中的某些板块。我想这就是你所说的那个‘限速’。债券抛售的速度，加上

turns.en: with the fact that the earnings tailwinds have been moderating, has meant that equities have started to consolidate a bit. So, I wanted to unpack these two parts of this and kind of separate them. Well, first I want to talk about the innovation part, and then I want to get to the bond… kind of the speed limit part.
turns.zh: 盈利顺风一直在减弱这一事实，意味着股票已经开始进入某种盘整。所以，我想把这两个部分拆开、分别来谈。嗯，首先我想谈谈创新这一部分，然后再谈到债券……那个‘限速’的部分。

turns.en: Carlyle wrote a recent report, which you may have kind of read, which came out a couple weeks ago, which really kind of unpacks the earnings growth and talks about where is it coming from, is it sustainable? Should we be looking at this as real earnings growth that's sustainable kind of real earnings growth? And again,
turns.zh: Carlyle（凯雷）最近发布了一份报告，你或许读过，大约几周前出的，它着实拆解了盈利增长，并探讨这些增长来自何处、是否可持续。我们是否应当把它视为真实且可持续的盈利增长？我再说一次，

turns.en: it's just people, go read the report, but it really speaks to two parts. One, how much of the earnings is being is just asset appreciation that's happening under the hood. Right? That's just a function of Anthropic going from US$380 billion to US$2 trillion, and all these stocks appreciating and then being marked as earnings, that's
turns.zh: 大家去读读那份报告就好，但它其实讲到了两个部分。其一，有多少盈利其实只是底层正在发生的资产增值。对吧？那不过是Anthropic从3800亿美元估值涨到2万亿美元、所有这些股票升值然后被计为盈利的一个函数，这是

turns.en: one. But two, they then go into, okay, because of this boom in underlying liquidity that's coming into the market, specifically narrowly to this part of the market, which is then one to one going into CapEx. Right? How much of that CapEx is now being depreciated forward? How much of it is actual real earnings as opposed to
turns.zh: 第一点。但第二点，他们接着谈到，好，由于涌入市场的这种底层流动性的热潮——尤其是狭窄地涌入市场的这一部分——然后一对一地进入了资本开支（CapEx）。对吧？这些资本开支中有多少如今正在被向前折旧（depreciated forward）？其中有多少是真正的真实盈利，而不是

turns.en: kind of the sugar rush? I want you to kind of think, talk through that. How do you think about it? Again, they came out on the side of, it's really just a sugar rush that is not sustainable. I'd like to hear your thoughts, if you believe that. So much of it gets painted as AI is causing all of this productivity gains that are
turns.zh: 那种‘糖分冲击’（sugar rush）？我想让你好好思考一下，谈谈这个。你怎么看？再说一次，他们的结论倾向于认为，这其实只是一场不可持续的‘糖分冲击’。我很想听听你的看法，你是否认同。之所以这么多东西被描绘成是AI在造成所有这些生产力增益，从而

turns.en: driving this earnings boom. Right? That's really kind of what you hear in the media most of the time. Obviously, I understand that view. I use AI day in, day out, clearly. I think that's why the media, everybody is so enamored with this view, that we're in this productivity boom. But I'd love to hear your thoughts. Do
turns.zh: 驱动了这场盈利繁荣。对吧？这真的算是你在媒体上最常听到的说法。显然，我理解这种观点。我显然每天都在用AI。我认为这就是为什么媒体、每个人都如此着迷于这种观点，觉得我们正处在这场生产力繁荣之中。但我很想听听你的看法。你

turns.en: you think that's true? And if so, why? And do you have any data that maybe backs that up on your own? Yeah, I think you're right. The problem about every technology kind of revolution is it goes in phases. The first phase is like the investment phase, and we've seen a lot of that. I think
turns.zh: 认为这是真的吗？如果是，为什么？你自己有没有什么数据可以佐证？——是的，我觉得你说得对。每一场技术革命的问题都在于它是分阶段推进的。第一阶段就像投资阶段，这方面我们已经见到了很多。我认为

turns.en: AI CapEx boosting semiconductor and kind of AI CapEx beneficiary earnings. And the problem is you cannot extrapolate the investment phase for too long. This kind of investment phase might be one of the largest and longest we've seen in history with regards to how much it is as a proportion of GDP growth. But
turns.zh: AI资本开支正在提振半导体以及AI资本开支受益者的盈利。而问题在于，你无法把投资阶段外推（extrapolate）太久。就其占GDP增长的比例而言，这一轮投资阶段可能是我们历史上所见到的规模最大、持续时间最长的之一。但

turns.en: nevertheless, the market is already, to your point, starting to question a bit, how much you should extrapolate the type of level of earnings and the type of earnings growth that you've been generating linked to investment. So, the second phase is then the kind of application phase where the applications
turns.zh: 尽管如此，正如你所说，市场已经开始有点质疑：对于与投资挂钩所创造出的那种盈利水平和那种盈利增长，你应该外推到什么程度。所以，第二阶段就是所谓的应用阶段（application phase），届时这些应用

turns.en: really get rolled out and that leads into the adoption phase. And the big problem is that often you have this J curve where the actual productivity growth and the benefits take a long time. So, you have this J curve. And I would say that we are probably still at the early part of the J curve. We need to be honest, it's pretty
turns.zh: 真正得到推广铺开，进而进入采用阶段（adoption phase）。而最大的问题在于，你往往会出现这条J曲线（J curve）——真正的生产力增长和收益需要很长时间才能显现。所以你有这条J曲线。我会说，我们很可能仍处于J曲线的早期阶段。我们必须诚实，就

turns.en: early in terms of saying that we can really see the productivity benefits in corporate earnings in kind of like broader macro measures of productivity. But I think there's some early signs. I mean you have occasionally like CEOs potentially quantifying cost savings. You obviously have all of us using AI in our work and
turns.zh: 我们能否在企业盈利中、在更宏观的生产力衡量指标中真正看到生产力收益而言，现在还很早。但我认为已经出现了一些早期迹象。我是说，你偶尔会看到CEO们可能在量化成本节约。显然，我们所有人在工作和

turns.en: in our lives and there's definitely some benefits to it. But I would agree with you, with regards to the AI boom, you're entering now a phase that's potentially less tangible. Like I think what was really quite nice in the AI CapEx boom is that it was very earnings driven and it was, to some extent, quarter to quarter the
turns.zh: 生活中都在使用AI，它确实带来了一些好处。但就AI繁荣而言，我同意你的看法，你正进入一个可能不那么‘可触可感’的阶段。我认为AI资本开支繁荣中非常美妙的一点在于，它非常由盈利驱动，而且在一定程度上，市场能够一个季度接一个季度地

turns.en: market could kind of pay for those earnings. Whereas now, I think you're right, like you're going a bit away from the earnings linkage, maybe a bit more towards understanding what applications potential could be in the future. So, you have like companies launch applications, and then the market needs to make an assessment
turns.zh: 为这些盈利买单。而现在，我认为你说得对，你正有点脱离与盈利的挂钩，也许更多地转向去理解应用在未来的潜力。所以现在的情况是，公司推出应用，然后市场需要做出评估——

turns.en: how successful these applications can be, what revenue, what profit they can bring, and also who are the losers and the winners. So, like more dispersion to some extent within tech, but also within the broader economy. But I think our kind of macro team's forecasts, with regards to productivity
turns.zh: 这些应用能有多成功、能带来什么收入和利润，以及谁是输家、谁是赢家。所以在一定程度上，科技板块内部、乃至更广泛的经济内部，都出现了更大的分化（dispersion）。但我认为我们宏观团队对未来十年左右生产力

turns.en: growth benefits in the next decade or so, are still material. There's still a lot up for grabs. The challenge is just that in a very near term I would agree with you, we cannot really see it.
turns.zh: 增长收益的预测，仍然是相当可观的。仍有很大的空间可以去争取。挑战只是在于，在非常近的短期内，我同意你的看法，我们还真的看不到它。

turns.en: Yeah. And honestly, I think people naturally see those earnings numbers and they assume this is kind of some operational earnings growth. And it really isn't operational news. Actually, cash flows from these hyperscalers is falling out of bed. Right? Meanwhile they are the primary contributor to these earnings growth.
turns.zh: 是啊。老实说，我认为人们自然而然地看到那些盈利数字，就假定这是某种运营层面的盈利增长。而它其实并不是运营层面的消息。实际上，这些超大规模云计算公司（hyperscalers）的现金流正在急剧恶化。对吧？与此同时，它们却是这些盈利增长的主要贡献者。

turns.en: Right? When you look at it, it's almost, if you look at a chart of the two, they are normally highly correlated. Right? You'd imagine cash flow getting kicked off from earnings and yet the two cannot be more apart. And the amount of debt that is being taken on, as you know, and
turns.zh: 对吧？当你去看时，几乎——如果你把两者的图表放在一起看，它们通常是高度相关的。对吧？你会以为现金流是从盈利中派生出来的，然而两者却从未如此背离。而且正如你所知，正在被承担的债务规模，以及

turns.en: the credit issues that come with it, as you've already highlighted, are very structural. It's hard to look at that. And yes, we can gloss over and say, yeah, earnings growth makes these current valuations maybe worthwhile. But it's hard to kind of believe that if you really dig more than kind of three feet underground.
turns.zh: 随之而来的信用问题——你已经强调过了——都是非常结构性的。很难直视这一点。是的，我们可以轻描淡写地说，是啊，盈利增长让这些当前的估值或许还算值得。但如果你真的深挖超过‘三英尺’，就很难相信这一点了。

turns.en: I think that's important, what you mentioned. Do you think we're in a bit of a bubble in that sense? I would say it's important what you mentioned there in the sense that the market agrees with you. I think most investors we speak to, they're already discounting those earnings quite
turns.zh: 我认为你提到的那点很重要。从这个意义上说，你认为我们是不是有点身处泡沫之中？——我会说，你在那里提到的一点很重要，意思就是市场是认同你的。我认为我们交谈过的大多数投资者，他们已经在相当程度上对这些盈利打了折扣。

turns.en: a bit. And this is important if you look at the kind of valuations of the semiconductor companies, if you look, in general, at valuations of the tech complex, they've derated a lot year-to-date. What you actually will find is the 12-month forward PE ratio for the MSCI world will have come down 15% or so year to date. So,
turns.zh: 而且这一点很重要——如果你去看半导体公司的估值，如果你总体上去看整个科技板块的估值，它们今年以来已经大幅去估值（derated）。你实际会发现，MSCI全球指数（MSCI World）的12个月远期市盈率（forward PE）今年迄今已经下降了大约15%。所以，

turns.en: that shows you the market doesn't completely pay for the earnings and the earnings growth. And for the S&P 500, I think when we came into the year, 12-month forward PE ratio was 23 times, now you're at 19 times. So, I would agree the market is already, to some extent, discounting some of these highly cyclical earnings
turns.zh: 这表明市场并没有完全为这些盈利和盈利增长买单。而对于标普500（S&P 500），我认为我们年初进来时，12个月远期市盈率是23倍，现在你处在19倍。所以，我同意市场已经在一定程度上对这些高度周期性的盈利打了折扣，

turns.en: because you're absolutely right, the business models that are generating, currently, a large amount of the earnings, are very cyclical businesses. And that's to some extent what you have to be a bit careful with. Because just like earnings can go up a lot, they can also come down a lot. But what I would say
turns.zh: 因为你完全正确，当前创造大量盈利的那些商业模式，是非常周期性的业务。而这在某种程度上就是你需要有点小心的地方。因为正如盈利可以大幅上涨，它们也可以大幅下跌。但我会说

turns.en: though is that some of these kind of data center construction and compute contracts, they're quite long-dated, it's quite unusual. So, that's why, to some extent, you have a bit more visibility than normal. And that's why investors are to some extent not worried yet. But I agree with you. At some point there's two major
turns.zh: 的是，其中一些数据中心建设和算力（compute）合同，它们的期限相当长，这很不寻常。所以这就是为什么你在一定程度上比平常拥有更多的可见度。这也是为什么投资者在某种程度上还不担心。但我同意你的看法。在某个时点，有两个重大

turns.en: questions that you have to ask. How much compute do we need and what's the price for it based on the capacity and the type of technology advances that we will find. I think as of now, our team, both in the technology, equity research, but also all strategists, they've been looking at this and they find that because you're
turns.zh: 问题你必须去问。我们需要多少算力，以及基于我们将发现的产能和技术进步的类型，它的价格应该是多少。我认为到目前为止，我们的团队——无论是科技股票研究团队，还是所有的策略师——他们一直在研究这个问题，他们发现，因为你正

turns.en: going from these kind of like LLM development compute demands, like frontier models, to applications, there's a good chance that the demand for compute in the near term is still going to remain quite high.
